basics.description:
Deploy **UTL-X Transformation Engine — Professional** into your Azure subscription.

**Professional plan:** 32 worker threads, up to 10 auto-scaling instances. Handles 50+ integrations at ~160K msg/s.

Billing is handled automatically through your Azure bill. A 14-day free trial is included.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Azure region for all resources. Choose a region close to your workloads.

options.text: [concat('Suggested admin key (copy this): **', guid(), '**  — Paste it into the Admin API Key field below and save it in a password manager. You can also choose your own key (minimum 8 characters).')]

elements.name: adminKey
elements.toolTip: Protects the Admin API and Web UI. Use the suggested UUID above, or enter your own (minimum 8 characters). Save it securely — it cannot be retrieved after deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: The admin key must be at least 8 characters.

options.text: Save this key securely — it cannot be retrieved after deployment. If you lose it, you can reset it with: az containerapp secret set --name <app> -g <rg> --secrets admin-key=<new-key>, then restart the container.

Professional plan: 32 concurrent worker threads, up to 10 auto-scaling instances. Transforms JSON, XML, CSV, YAML, and OData natively with 650+ stdlib functions, schema validation, and pipeline chaining. Ideal for production workloads with multiple integration flows.

elements.name: cpuCores
elements.label: CPU Cores per instance
elements.toolTip: CPU allocation per container instance. With 32 workers, 2.0+ cores is recommended.

elements.name: memoryGi
elements.label: Memory per instance
elements.toolTip: Memory allocation per container instance. With 32 workers processing concurrently, 4 GB+ is recommended.

allowedValues.label: 8 GB — messages up to 1 MB+ (large payloads)

options.text: XML and JSON messages expand 10-50x in memory during transformation (UDM parsing). With 32 concurrent workers, each processing a message, memory usage scales linearly. For messages over 500 KB, use 8 GB.

elements.name: minReplicas
elements.label: Minimum instances
elements.toolTip: Set to 0 for scale-to-zero (no cost when idle, ~10s cold start). Set to 1 for always-on (recommended for production).

elements.name: maxReplicas
elements.label: Maximum instances
elements.toolTip: Maximum number of instances for auto-scaling under load. Professional plan supports up to 10.

options.text: Without persistent storage the engine keeps transformations in memory only: they are lost on every restart and must be re-uploaded through the Admin API. Enabling it mounts an Azure Files share at /utlxe/data, so uploads survive restarts — and a .utlar bundle placed on the share starts the engine in locked mode, where transformations come from CI/CD and the Admin API refuses changes.

elements.name: enablePersistentStorage
elements.label: Persistent storage
elements.toolTip: Creates a Standard_LRS storage account and a 100 GiB file share in this resource group, mounted at /utlxe/data.

allowedValues.label: Disabled — in-memory only, re-upload after every restart

options.text: By default your application posts messages to UTLXe over HTTP. Choose Azure Service Bus to have the engine consume from a queue and publish results to a topic on its own, with auto-scaling driven by queue depth.

elements.name: messagingMode
elements.label: How messages reach UTLXe
elements.toolTip: HTTP: your application calls the engine. Azure Service Bus: the engine consumes from a queue you own and publishes results to a topic you own.
elements.defaultValue: HTTP only — your application calls UTLXe

allowedValues.label: HTTP only — your application calls UTLXe
Azure Service Bus — queue in, topic out

elements.name: serviceBusConnection
elements.toolTip: A connection string for your Service Bus namespace with Send and Listen rights. The namespace, queue and topic must already exist — this offer does not create them.

constraints.validationMessage: Paste the full connection string, starting with Endpoint=sb://

elements.name: inputQueueName
elements.label: Input queue name
elements.toolTip: The existing queue UTLXe consumes from.

elements.name: outputTopicName
elements.label: Output topic name
elements.toolTip: The existing topic UTLXe publishes transformed messages to.

options.text: Name your transformation 'servicebus-input' when you upload it. Messages arriving on the queue are routed to the transformation whose name matches the input binding, so a differently named transformation leaves messages consumed but not transformed.
